source_en_display: ENGLAND\nThe Age of Expansion coincided with a period of {religious strife} in England. The Church of England--theoretically a Protestant denomination but maintaining many Catholic traditions--faced a series of challenges during the colonial period from would-be reformers, or {Puritans}. The English monarchy shifted its support between pro-Catholic and various Protestant factions from generation to generation, and the English Civil War (1640-49) resulted in the execution of Charles I and a period of Puritan rule (1649-60) under Oliver Cromwell. With so much religious conflict at home, the English government had neither the desire nor the ability to enforce religious conformity in its colonial possessions. The colonies became havens of {religious freedom} for groups (e.g. Puritans, Anabaptists, Quakers) who faced persecution in the Old World.
zh_hant_draft: 英國\n擴張時代恰逢英國的{宗教衝突}。英格蘭教會名義上屬於新教，卻保留許多天主教傳統；殖民時期，主張改革的{清教徒}不斷向它提出挑戰。英國王室對親天主教派與不同新教派的支持，隨世代更迭而轉變。英國內戰（1640至1649年）導致查理一世遭處決，隨後在奧利佛克倫威爾領導下，進入清教徒統治時期（1649至1660年）。本土宗教紛爭不斷，英國政府既無意願，也無能力要求殖民領地信奉同一宗教。殖民領地因此成為清教徒、再洗禮派、貴格會等在舊世界遭受迫害群體追求{宗教自由}的避風港。

source_en_display: FRANCE\nLatecomers to the New World, France established her first secure American colonies in {Canada} along the St. Lawrence river, where the harsh northern climate proved more suitable for the {fur trade} than for large-scale agricultural endeavors. The French found the {Great Lakes Indians} to be ideal partners in the fur trade and formed long-term trading relationships with the Hurons, Algonquins and other tribes. Though French forts, missions, and trading posts soon dotted the Great Lakes region, French settlements were generally small enough to operate in relative {harmony} with the local native population. Although this relationship was not entirely without incident, the French were often able to cooperate profitably with the natives. This cooperation occasionally extended into the military realm.
zh_hant_draft: 法國\n法國較晚進入新世界，沿聖羅倫斯河在{加拿大}建立了首批穩固的美洲殖民領地。當地嚴寒的北方氣候，比起大規模農業，更適合{毛皮貿易}。法國人發現{五大湖印地安人}是毛皮貿易的理想夥伴，於是與休倫人、阿爾岡昆人及其他部落建立長期貿易關係。法國的堡壘、傳教所與貿易站很快遍布五大湖地區；但法國居住地通常規模不大，因此能與當地原住民相對{和睦共處}。這段關係並非全無摩擦，法國人仍經常能與原住民合作獲利，有時更將合作延伸到軍事領域。

source_en_display: FRANCE\nTo reflect the superior ability of the French to cooperate with the native population, the French player's colonies and units cause {alarm} among the Indians at only {half} the rate of other European powers.

source_en_display: SPAIN\nIn 1492, the same year that Columbus discovered America, the Spanish completed their centuries-long "reconquista" of the Iberian peninsula from the Muslim Moors. This victory left Spain with a generation of {military men} spoiling for a new avenue of expansion and more eager than ever to bring Christianity to the {heathen} at the point of a sword. The New World and its unsuspecting natives provided exactly such an opportunity, and the history of the first century of Spanish expansion in America is the history of the conquest, plunder, and destruction of countless Native American civilizations. The Spanish were the first Europeans to encounter the 'Indians,' and the otherwise mighty {Aztec} and {Inca} empires proved psychologically unprepared for the arrival of an alien power armed with muskets and thirsty for conquest. Conquistador {Hernan Cortes} arrived at Veracruz in 1519 with a few hundred men and, within two years, brought the Aztec Empire to its knees.
zh_hant_draft: 西班牙\n1492年，哥倫布發現美洲；同年，西班牙人完成了歷時數百年、從穆斯林摩爾人手中收復伊比利半島的「收復失地運動」。這場勝利使西班牙擁有一代渴望尋找新擴張途徑的{軍人}，也更急於以刀劍向{異教徒}傳播基督教。新世界及毫無防備的原住民，恰好提供了這樣的機會。西班牙在美洲擴張的第一個世紀，見證了無數美洲原住民文明遭到征服、掠奪與摧毀。西班牙人是最早接觸「印地安人」的歐洲人；即使強大的{阿茲特克}與{印加}帝國，在心理上也沒有準備好面對一個配備火槍、渴望征服的陌生勢力。征服者{埃爾南科爾特斯}於1519年率領數百人抵達韋拉克魯斯，不到兩年便迫使阿茲特克帝國屈服。
notes: 征服者姓名與地名譯法待術語審查；原文的 heathen 與加引號的 Indians 帶殖民時代視角；原版檔案來源與正常路徑 A／B 印字已驗；中文排版尚未驗

source_en_display: SPAIN\nTo reflect the strategic surprise which Spain achieved over pre-Columbian American civilizations, the Spanish player receives a {50%% combat bonus} when {attacking Indian villages}.

source_en_display: NETHERLANDS\nThe Protestant Dutch provinces gained their independence from Catholic Spain during the Age of Expansion. A maritime country of {fishermen} and {merchants}, the Dutch Netherlands operated large merchant and fishing fleets in the North Sea and the Baltic. Upon achieving political independence in the early seventeenth century, this tiny nation found itself ideally poised to expand its {overseas trade} into lucrative new markets in the Far East and New World. Unlike their rivals and sometime enemies the Spanish, French, and English, the Dutch were ruled by their merchant class. This unique arrangement led them to focus all aspects of state diplomatic, military, and economic policy around the {interests of trade}. Their strategy proved quite successful, and the Dutch economy and merchant fleet expanded so rapidly that the other European powers felt compelled to take drastic measures against the Dutch in order to prop up their own less successful enterprises.
zh_hant_draft: 荷蘭\n擴張時代，荷蘭的新教諸省脫離天主教西班牙，取得獨立。荷蘭是由{漁民}與{商人}構成的海洋國家，在北海與波羅的海經營龐大的商船隊和漁船隊。十七世紀初取得政治獨立後，這個小國恰好具備向遠東與新世界的獲利市場拓展{海外貿易}的有利條件。與西班牙、法國和英國這些競爭對手、有時也是敵人的國家不同，荷蘭由商人階層主導。這種獨特安排，使荷蘭外交、軍事與經濟政策的各方面都圍繞{貿易利益}運作。這項策略相當成功：荷蘭經濟與商船隊迅速擴張，迫使其他歐洲強權對荷蘭採取激烈措施，以扶持本國較不成功的商業事業。
notes: 標題沿用既有荷蘭譯名；荷蘭的新教諸省對應 Protestant Dutch provinces；原版檔案來源與正常路徑 A／B 印字已驗；中文排版尚未驗

source_en_display: NETHERLANDS\nTo represent the strength of the Dutch economy, as well as Dutch achievements in shipping, commerce, and banking, the Dutch player receives a bonus when trading with Amsterdam. {Commodity prices} in Amsterdam {do not collapse} as quickly as in other European ports and they {recover} more quickly.
zh_hant_draft: 荷蘭\n為反映荷蘭經濟，以及航運、商業和銀行業的成就，荷蘭玩家在阿姆斯特丹交易時享有一項優勢：當地的{商品價格}{不會像其他歐洲港口那樣迅速崩跌}，而且{回升}得更快。
